pointwise.question: Can the report's key method and study claims be traced to identifiable publications or reviewable derivations?

anchors.1: Key research claims have no identifiable basis.
anchors.2: Only generic references to papers or experiments.
anchors.3: Publications exist but the attribution of important solutions or results is ambiguous.
anchors.4: Important claims map to identifiable publications or derivations, with minor citation-scope gaps.
anchors.5: Study identities, proposed methods and claimed results have clear source relationships; estimates and derivations expose their assumptions.

pointwise.boundary: An adequate title/author/publication record can work without a URL. A published preprint must not be described as peer-reviewed without basis. Locatability is not support.

provenance.change_note: Adds source linkage across the requested studies; challenge PT items check that a study response is included.

pointwise.title: Support within completed verification
pointwise.question: Within the recorded completed checks, do method classifications, study descriptions and claimed results agree with evidence?

anchors.1: A central checked claim is contradicted, undermining the report.
anchors.2: Several important checked claims have material support errors.
anchors.3: Support is mixed, with a consequential scope or attribution error.
anchors.4: Important checked claims hold, with only minor qualification errors.
anchors.5: All assessed claims match the obtained evidence in setting, method and strength; unassessed claims remain unverified.

pointwise.boundary: Record selected/completed checks. Retrieval failure is an execution issue, not a low score or NA; retry or defer this check if nothing can be assessed. Official rubric facts are not externally verified by inclusion here.

provenance.change_note: Locally added limited-scope evidence audit; avoids treating exact reported percentages as automatically true.

pointwise.title: Queueing-based scaling
pointwise.question: Does the report explain queueing/performance models for scaling, their benefits and assumptions?

anchors.1: No queueing-based method.
anchors.2: Only names queueing theory.
anchors.3: Explains some queueing quantities, but the capacity-decision principle, interpretable performance benefit or model-assumption limitation is substantively missing.
anchors.4: Connects arrivals/service, response time or queue length, capacity action and assumptions with minor detail missing.
anchors.5: Explains how queueing models estimate service-objective capacity, their interpretable performance benefits and how nonstationarity/model mismatch limits them, with adaptation where relevant.

pointwise.boundary: Do not claim queueing is inherently static-only. No mandatory MDP or particular queue model.

provenance.change_note: Restore a mainstream family; particular models remain replaceable. Cross-review makes missing principle, benefit or limitation symmetric at 3.

pointwise.title: Reinforcement-learning control
pointwise.question: Does the report explain RL scaling as sequential policy learning, with benefits and limitations?

anchors.1: No RL method.
anchors.2: Only names an agent or AI.
anchors.3: Explains some RL components, but the interaction/cumulative-objective principle, adaptive-control benefit or training/exploration limitation is substantively missing.
anchors.4: Explains state/action/reward learning, adaptive benefit and training/exploration limits with minor detail missing.
anchors.5: Explains policy learning from environment feedback toward cumulative objectives, adaptive decisions and sample, safety, reward-design or nonstationarity limitations.

pointwise.boundary: No required RL architecture; classify implementation rather than all RL as proactive. A policy is not necessarily a workload predictor.

provenance.change_note: Restore a mainstream family; particular models remain replaceable. Cross-review makes missing principle, benefit or limitation symmetric at 3.

pointwise.title: Fuzzy-control scaling
pointwise.question: Does the report explain fuzzy scaling, its advantages and limitations?

anchors.1: No fuzzy-control method.
anchors.2: Only uses high/medium/low labels.
anchors.3: Explains some fuzzy inputs/rules, but rule-to-resource action, usefulness for imprecise inputs or rule/tuning limitation is substantively missing.
anchors.4: Explains graded membership/rules to action, control benefits and tuning limits with minor detail missing.
anchors.5: Explains how graded linguistic conditions and rule combination produce resource actions, why useful for imprecise inputs, and how membership/rule design, stability or adaptation limits use.

pointwise.boundary: No fixed membership function or paper. Fuzzy control may be reactive or anticipatory depending on inputs.

provenance.change_note: Restore a mainstream family; particular models remain replaceable. Cross-review makes missing principle, benefit or limitation symmetric at 3.

pointwise.title: Time-series prediction
pointwise.question: Does the report explain time-series scaling, its benefits and limits?

anchors.1: No time-series approach.
anchors.2: Only says history predicts the future.
anchors.3: Explains some temporal modeling, but forecast-to-scaling use, readiness/resource benefit or pattern/error limitation is substantively missing.
anchors.4: Explains temporal patterns, advance action and error/change limits with minor detail missing.
anchors.5: Explains temporal dependence, trend or seasonality forecasts used ahead of provisioning, readiness/resource benefits and risks of pattern breaks, unsuitable horizons or forecast error.

pointwise.boundary: No mandatory ARIMA, Daedalus or 71% result. ML/time-series can overlap if the temporal principle is actually explained.

provenance.change_note: Restore a mainstream family; particular models remain replaceable. Cross-review makes missing principle, benefit or limitation symmetric at 3.

anchors.-1: B slightly better explains the relevant scaling behavior, although A may explain a local limitation better.

Compare opposing reactive/proactive reasoning advantages on the same consequential basis; equally strong opposing advantages yield 0.

provenance.change_note: Adapts timing and error trade-offs into conditional reasoning instead of fixed superiority claims. Cross-review distinguishes profile completion and equal opposing timing advantages.

drb2_58.title: 疫情高校在线学习效果
drb2_58.full_query:
Please conduct a systematic review of the effectiveness of online learning in higher education during the COVID-19 pandemic period (January 2020 to August 2023). Your review should answer two main questions: 1) To what extent is online learning effective? 2) What factors influenced its effectiveness?

To this end, you will first need to identify and summarize a range of relevant empirical studies published during this period. Then, based on these studies, your output must contain three sections:

1.  **Summary Table of Reviewed Studies:** Create a table summarizing the key empirical studies. This table must include the following columns in this specific order: Authors, Country, Sample Size, Research Design, Outcome Variable, and Finding on Effectiveness (i.e., whether the study found it effective, ineffective, or neutral). You must cover at least 15 different studies from the 2020-2023 period.

2.  **Effectiveness Analysis:** Synthesize the findings of the studies to draw an overall conclusion about the effectiveness of online learning. Your analysis should categorize the studies based on their research methodologies (e.g., cross-sectional perceptual surveys, cross-sectional comparative studies, longitudinal studies, randomized controlled trials), and discuss how the chosen methodology influenced the reported results. 3.  **Analysis of Influencing Factors:** Identify and elaborate on key factors that positively or negatively influenced the effectiveness of online learning during the pandemic. For each factor, you must explain the mechanism through which it impacted learning effectiveness. drb2_66.full_query:
I've recently been focusing on colorectal cancer (CRC) treatment, and I've heard that gut microbiota significantly impacts treatment efficacy and side effects. I would like you to conduct a comprehensive research and summary for me, covering publicly available research findings up to September 2024. Please help me organize a table specifically outlining the interactions between gut microbiota and various CRC treatment methods. This table needs to include the following columns: 'Treatment Area', 'Specific Modality', 'Positive Impacts/Advantages', 'Negative Impacts/Complications'. Under 'Treatment Area', please make sure to cover surgery, chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and radiotherapy. Additionally, I'd like to understand some future directions, so please include probiotics/prebiotics and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as 'Specific Modalities' under 'Future Outlook'. drb2_71.title: 相信阴谋论的心理动机
drb2_71.full_query:
我正在研究阴谋论的心理学，希望你能帮我完成一份文献综述，具体要求如下：
1. 这份综述需要基于2017年及以前发表的学术研究。
2. 首先，请总结出驱动人们相信阴谋论的几种主要的心理动机或需求类型。
3. 然后，针对你总结出的每一种动机类型，请详细阐述以下三点：
    a) 吸引力来源：为什么阴谋论对于有这种动机的人来说，会显得特别有吸引力？
    b) 易感人群特征：哪些特定人群、性格特质、或处于何种情境下的人，更容易因为这种动机而去相信阴谋论？请结合具体研究发现来说明。
    c) 实际后果：根据研究，相信阴谋论最终是否能够真正满足人们的这些动机？它会带来哪些实际的心理或行为层面的后果？

drb2_75.title: 剑桥中国文学史理论革新
drb2_75.full_query:
我正在研究关于中国文学史写作的学术争论，特别是围绕2010年出版的《剑桥中国文学史》（The Cambridge History of Chinese Literature）及其主编之一宇文所安（Stephen Owen）的理论。我希望你帮我深入调研并整理一份报告，清晰地梳理出这场争论的核心。具体来说，报告需要包含以下几个部分：

1.  **传统方法的批判**：总结宇文所安等人认为传统或主流的中国文学史写作存在哪些问题。请具体阐述这些传统方法背后的几个核心观念或原则。

2.  **新理论的提出**：阐述宇文所安为回应上述问题，提出了哪些具有颠覆性的新编纂原则和观念。请详细解释这些新观念的核心思想，例如“史中之史”（history of history）等。

3.  **新历史主义的影响**：分析“新历史主义”（New Historicism），特别是斯蒂芬·格林布拉特（Stephen Greenblatt）的理论，是如何影响《剑桥中国文学史》的。请说明新历史主义的哪些核心概念（如“文本的历史性”和“历史的文本性”）被运用于这部文学史中，并如何将研究视角从“文学”转向“文学文化”。

4.  **“中国性”的重塑**：解释《剑桥中国文学史》是如何重新定义“中国文学”和“中国性”（Chineseness）这一概念的。说明它为何从“民族国家”转向“社群”作为界定标准，这对文学史的语言和地理范围产生了什么影响，并给出一个具体的章节例子来说明这种变化。

请确保你的报告结构清晰，分点阐述，语言学术化且易于理解。报告的目的是梳理和呈现《剑桥中国文学史》所代表的理论革新，而非评价其成功与否。

Please put this rule in your task plan and keep it in your memory: **During the research process, you are not allowed to view the following article and urls: {'title': 'Is a New Chinese Literary History Possible? A Critical Investigation of The Cambridge History of Chinese Literature', 'authors': ['Shen Yifan 沈一帆'], 'urls': ['https://www.sciencedirect.com/org/science/article/pii/S2352133324000104', 'https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379985497_Is_a_New_Chinese_Literary_History_Possible_A_Critical_Investigation_of_The_Cambridge_History_of_Chinese_Literature', 'https://www.lhp.sdu.edu.cn/info/1372/4096.htm', 'https://brill.com/view/journals/joch/10/1/article-p1_1.xml]}. pointwise.title: 研究对象与呈现目的
pointwise.question: 报告是否以2010年《剑桥中国文学史》及宇文所安等人的理论革新为对象，而非转向裁判其成败？

anchors.1: 主体不是该书或相关理论。
anchors.2: 主体转为个人褒贬，理论梳理仅零散出现。
anchors.3: 对象正确，但有明显成败裁判挤占理论说明，或主编与全书意见归属混淆。
anchors.4: 主要为理论梳理，对象与宇文所安角色清楚，只有局部不必要评价。
anchors.5: 书、2010年出版背景及宇文所安作为主编之一的角色明确，全文服务理论呈现；必要争论背景不变为作者判决。

pointwise.boundary: 不要求赞美理论，不禁止说明概念适用边界；有据质疑归属属于准确呈现而非题外裁判。

anchors.3: 开端发展结局或新断代/多线索作用只说一侧，或未解释问题。
anchors.4: 旧叙事预设与新组织变化清楚，少量范围欠缺。
anchors.5: 说明线性发展叙事的方向/终点预设及其所受批判，解释重新断代、多层或多线索如何改变文学史组织。

pointwise.question: 报告是否解释史中之史如何研究文学过去被后人筛选、保存和重述的过程？

anchors.1: 无史中之史。
anchors.2: 只列术语或称历史被建构。
anchors.3: 有建构论但筛选重述过程或研究对象变化不清。

drb2_76.title: International organizations and decolonization
drb2_76.full_query:
Hello, I am researching the complex relationship between international organizations and decolonization in the 20th century. I hope you can help me compile a detailed report, with a deadline until early 2022. The report needs to clearly outline this history and be divided into three main parts:

Part One, regarding the period from after World War I until the end of World War II. Please focus on the dual role of the League of Nations in decolonization. On the one hand, please explain how the League maintained imperial interests through the Mandates System; on the other hand, also explain how it inadvertently provided a stage for international oversight of colonial affairs. Additionally, please introduce anti-imperialist organizations that emerged during the same period and stood in opposition to the League, especially the "League Against Imperialism", detailing its founding background, main activities, and impact.

Part Two, regarding the period of the United Nations after World War II. Please outline the role of the United Nations in the process of decolonization. This section needs to include: the United Nations' initial stance on colonial issues at its founding, the evolution from the League of Nations' Mandates System to the United Nations' Trusteeship System, and the provisions in the UN Charter concerning non-self-governing territories. Please explain in particular detail how the United Nations General Assembly and its subsidiary committees (e.g., the "Committee on Information from Non-Self-Governing Territories") became the main arena for anti-colonial struggles, and explain the historical significance and main content of the 1960 "Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples."

Part Three, regarding the impact of decolonization on international organizations themselves. Please analyze how the large number of former colonial states joining the United Nations changed the agenda and power dynamics of the UN and other international organizations. Specifically, explain how international issues shifted from an "East-West confrontation" to a "North-South divide", and introduce the rise of the "Non-Alignment Movement" and the "Group of 77", as well as the background and objectives of their promotion of a "New International Economic Order" (NIEO). At the same time, also briefly mention how decolonization spurred new functions for the United Nations, such as peacekeeping operations.

Throughout the report, please use clear language, avoid simplistic dichotomies of praise or condemnation, and demonstrate the complexity of the relationship between the two. Thank you!

**important**The following is a rule of highest priority that you must not violate. Please put this rule in your task plan and keep it in your memory: **During the research process, you are not allowed to view the following article and urls: {'title': 'Special issue introduction: Towards a global history of international organizations and decolonization', 'authors': ['Eva-Maria Muschik'], 'urls': ['https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-global-history/article/special-issue-introduction-towards-a-global-history-of-international-organizations-and-decolonization/066AFEF8CEA16E7F776CC7CFF72927CC', 'https://ideas.repec.org/a/cup/jglhis/v17y2022i2p173-190_1.html', 'https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359174525_Special_issue_introduction_Towards_a_global_history_of_international_organizations_and_decolonization', 'https://ucrisportal.univie.ac.at/en/publications/towards-a-global-history-of-international-organizations-and-decol']}. Even if you accidentally read it, please ignore the content of the article and do not quote it.**

pointwise.title: The League's dual role
pointwise.question: Does the report describe both the Mandates System's protection of imperial interests and the opening it created for international scrutiny?

anchors.1: Neither role is described.
anchors.2: Only praises or condemns the League without a concrete institutional account.
anchors.3: One role is concrete but the other is absent or merely asserted, or the mandates' welfare/development justification is omitted despite describing administration and scrutiny.
anchors.4: Both roles and their institutions are clear, with a minor territorial or procedural gap.
anchors.5: Identifies imperial administration under mandates, its stated welfare/development obligations and international reporting/review through the Permanent Mandates Commission, with territorial scope and limits clear.

pointwise.boundary: The two sides define the requested dual role; one strong side with the other missing scores 3. Explain the mandates' stated welfare/development obligations alongside imperial administration; identifying scrutiny alone does not explain that legitimating framework. Do not require named historians, British India or a fixed Article 22 quotation. Causal force is compared in PW.D3.01.

query_quotes: dual role of the League of Nations
provenance.change_note: Retain the institutional dual-role content, allowing explained qualifications; remove expert-name and exact-word requirements. Cross-review makes the already-required welfare/development framework explicit in 3/5 anchors.

pointwise.title: League Against Imperialism
pointwise.question: Does the report describe the LAI's founding context, activities and impact as an anti-imperialist organization?

anchors.1: The LAI is absent.
anchors.2: Only names the LAI or calls it anti-imperialist.
anchors.3: Founding context, activities or impact is missing, or organizational alliances/control tensions are omitted from the impact account.
anchors.4: All three are identifiable, with a minor date, actor or scope gap.
anchors.5: Explains founding setting, concrete international anti-imperialist organizing and impact, including how communist/Comintern support and organizational tensions affected reach and limitations without imposing a single cause of decline.

pointwise.boundary: Brussels 1927 and Comintern-linked organization are official checking leads, not authority to ignore better-supported qualifications. Do not require Berlin, Münzenberg or a predetermined single cause of decline. The LAI alone can satisfy the emphasized organization request without a fixed count of other groups.

query_quotes: founding background, main activities, and impact
provenance.change_note: v3.3 targeted revision: A strong founding and congress account cannot mask entirely missing organizational impact/tensions; retain one organization profile with explicit mixed grade.

pointwise.title: UN founding stance
pointwise.question: Does the report describe the UN's initial position on colonial rule at its founding?

anchors.1: No founding stance is described.
anchors.2: Only says the UN supported freedom or replaced the League.
anchors.3: Gives some founding context but does not identify the stance or compromises on colonial rule.
anchors.4: The initial stance and relevant compromise are clear, with minor context gaps.
anchors.5: The report explains the 1945 founding settlement's position on colonial rule and its institutional continuities with the League, distinguishing self-determination or welfare commitments from immediate universal independence and identifying the colonial-power context.

pointwise.boundary: No specific founding-city sentence is required. This checks an initial position, not the later evolution or a claim that the UN was wholly emancipatory or imperial.

query_quotes: the United Nations' initial stance on colonial issues at its founding
provenance.change_note: Use official founding context; query adds explicit colonial stance rather than merely date/place and institutional ancestry.

pointwise.title: Mandates to trusteeship
pointwise.question: Does the report describe the transition from League mandates to UN trusteeship and the relevant procedural changes?

anchors.1: No transition is described.
anchors.2: Only says trusteeship replaced mandates.
anchors.3: Names both systems but leaves their relationship or an important procedural difference unclear.
anchors.4: The relationship and oversight differences are clear with a minor territorial or procedural gap.
anchors.5: The report explains the institutional transition and the roles of petitions and visits in trusteeship, with territorial coverage and limits clear rather than implying every colony automatically became a trust territory.

pointwise.boundary: The relationship is one comparison, not separate name scores. Do not require an exhaustive trust-territory list or treat procedure as proof of inevitable independence.

query_quotes: the evolution from the League of Nations' Mandates System to the United Nations' Trusteeship System
provenance.change_note: Preserve transition and procedural distinction; locally guard against automatic all-colony transfer.

pointwise.title: Non-self-governing territory provisions
pointwise.question: Does the report explain the UN Charter provisions concerning non-self-governing territories?

anchors.1: No relevant Charter provisions.
anchors.2: Only names the Charter or colonial territories.
anchors.3: Identifies provisions but leaves their obligations, self-government objective or territory category unclear.
anchors.4: The provisions and category distinction are mostly clear.
anchors.5: Chapter XI's non-self-governing territory framework, administering-power responsibilities and information obligations are explained, distinguishing self-government from a blanket promise of immediate independence and from the trusteeship framework.

pointwise.boundary: Do not merge Chapter XI and trusteeship. Article numbers alone do not satisfy the item, and accurate paraphrase is acceptable.

query_quotes: provisions in the UN Charter concerning non-self-governing territories
provenance.change_note: Retain Charter substance while qualifying the official wording that blends non-self-governing territories with all trusteeships.

pointwise.title: General Assembly and committee arena
pointwise.question: Does the report explain in detail how the General Assembly and its subsidiary committees provided an arena for anti-colonial struggle?

anchors.1: No Assembly or committee role is described.
anchors.2: Only states that the UN opposed colonialism.
anchors.3: Assembly politics or information-committee review is absent or merely named, or the account omits how colonial information became open to international scrutiny.
anchors.4: Both Assembly politics and concrete committee procedures are described, with a minor institutional gap.
anchors.5: Explains Assembly coalition politics and the information committee's review of administering powers' economic, social and educational reporting, showing how this opened scrutiny and identifying institutional limits.

pointwise.boundary: No obligation to quote Pearson or force the Security Council deadlock as the sole cause. Distinguish the information committee and later declaration-implementation bodies; exact committee labels and dates require evidence, not blind reuse. Declaration-follow-up bodies are now checked separately in PT.D1.16; general committee detail cannot substitute for information scrutiny.

provenance.change_note: v3.3 targeted revision: Information flow and Assembly leverage stay connected, but separate declaration-follow-up function cannot be masked by good information review.

pointwise.title: The 1960 Declaration
pointwise.question: Does the report describe the 1960 Declaration's main content and historical significance?

anchors.1: The Declaration is absent.
anchors.2: Only names a 1960 resolution.
anchors.3: Describes either content or significance, but the other is absent or only a slogan.
anchors.4: Both are clear, with a minor ambiguity about scope or force.
anchors.5: Identifies the Declaration and explains self-determination, ending colonial subjection and transfer of authority, together with its historical political/normative significance and the distinction between declaration and implementation.

pointwise.boundary: Do not demand exact quotation or equate declaration with automatic enforcement. Only content/significance coverage here; the persuasiveness of institutional-change reasoning is compared separately.

query_quotes: historical significance and main content of the 1960
provenance.change_note: Retain the central declaration and transfer-of-power content; add coverage anchors and implementation boundary.

pointwise.title: New members and institutional power

anchors.2: Only says membership increased.
anchors.3: Describes membership growth but agenda or power consequences are missing, or discusses only the UN with no broader institutional connection.
anchors.4: Agenda and power changes are explicit, with a relevant broader organizational connection and a minor scope gap.
anchors.5: The report connects former colonies' entry with identifiable agenda and coalition/voting changes, distinguishes formal representation from other sources of power, and identifies effects beyond the UN alone.

pointwise.boundary: Do not require 51, 119 or nearly 50 as fixed numerical keys. A grounded UNCTAD or other relevant organizational connection is eligible; no prescribed list of agencies.

pointwise.title: East–West and North–South agendas

anchors.4: The changing prominence of inequality and development is clear with a minor period or scope gap.
anchors.5: Explains the increased prominence of development, economic inequality and trade relations relative to East–West conflict, identifying the actors and historical context without implying the Cold War simply ceased.

pointwise.boundary: The query's shift is not a demand for a total or uniform replacement thesis. Do not require the 1976 UNCTAD claim.

pointwise.title: NAM and G77

anchors.2: Only gives both names, or only mentions one without context.

anchors.4: Both formation contexts and roles are clear, with a minor chronological or institutional gap.
anchors.5: Both groupings' emergence and political/economic roles are explained, with identifiable formation contexts and their relationship without treating them as the same organization.

pointwise.boundary: Belgrade 1961 and the first UNCTAD/G77 setting in 1964 are checking leads; accurate explanation rather than exact wording is required. Bandung can provide context but is not a third compulsory profile.

anchors.4: Background, aims and promotion are clear, with a minor chronology or scope gap.
anchors.5: Explains economic grievances, collective promotion and concrete objectives for changing unequal international trade/economic relations, distinguishing national aid/development needs from structural reform claims and proposals from achieved outcomes.

drb2_79.title: 包容性日语教学
drb2_79.full_query:
我是一名大学的日语项目负责人，最近在考虑如何让我们的课堂对所有学生都更友好、更具包容性。我听说一些传统的日语教材和教学方法可能对LGBTQ+（性少数群体）的学生不太友好，比如总是默认学生是异性恋，或者在教性别化语言（男性语/女性语）时过于死板。我希望你帮我做一份调研报告，梳理一下这个问题。请重点关注截至2020年的情况，并整理成以下三个部分：

1.  **主流日语教材中的问题**：请调研几本在北美广泛使用的初中级日语教材，分析其中是否存在缺少LGBTQ+内容、或者包含一些基于异性恋假设的练习等问题。请务必举出具体来自哪本教材的例子，并说明为什么这些内容会给学生带来困扰。

2.  **日语性别化表达的教学挑战**：分析在日语教学中，关于男性和女性说话方式差异的传统教法存在哪些问题。请同样引用一些教材或教学指导书中的具体说法作为例子，并结合相关研究，说明这种教法为何可能是有问题的。

3.  **更具包容性的教学建议**：基于以上发现，提出一些老师们可以采纳的、具体的教学策略。比如，当教材内容有问题时如何处理？以及，如何以一种更包容的方式教授性别化语言？

请确保报告内容具体、有据可依，并清晰地分为以上三个部分。

Please put this rule in your task plan and keep it in your memory: **During the research process, you are not allowed to view the following article and urls: {'title': 'Toward More Inclusive Japanese Language Education: Incorporating an Awareness of Gender and Sexual Diversity among Students', 'authors': ['Jotaro Arimori'], 'urls': ['https://jll.pitt.edu/ojs/JLL/article/view/129', 'https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345454410_Toward_More_Inclusive_Japanese_Language_Education_Incorporating_an_Awareness_of_Gender_and_Sexual_Diversity_among_Students', 'https://doaj.org/article/c78fd6a300a34214beae90b10da5e355', 'https://doi.org/10.5195/jll.2020.129', 'https://www.jstor.org/stable/e27013670']}. Even if you accidentally read it, please ignore the content of the article and do not quote it.**

anchors.2: 只说自由表达或角色扮演，没有具体实践安排。
anchors.3: 有实践任务，但学生如何选择风格、运用语言或获得所需支持不清。
anchors.4: 实践步骤、风格选择及水平适配清楚，但如何理解表达效果或获得反馈仍不充分。
anchors.5: 给出目标水平可执行的表达任务和必要支持，允许自主选择角色或风格，并说明结合语境理解表达效果的反馈或反思安排，不按学生真实身份规定表达。

pointwise.boundary: 不限定中高级，不强制短剧、视频或身份探索；自愿使用虚构角色不等于被迫隐藏身份。水平适配可由任务难度与支持安排体现。本项检查实际运用，与PT.D1.12的观察理解分工；同一活动可覆盖两者，但需有各自具体任务，不凭重复的原则表述在两项得分。

drb2_84.title: 石油财富管理与资源诅咒
drb2_84.full_query:
I am researching how oil-dependent countries manage their wealth to avoid the 'resource curse'. Please help me compile a research report, primarily focusing on public information and academic views up to and including 2020. The report needs to include the following sections:
1.  **Core Challenges**: First, please explain what 'resource curse' and 'Dutch disease' are, and what specific negative impacts they have on the economies of oil-producing countries.
2.  **Fiscal Policy Strategies**: Outline and explain the three main fiscal policy rules discussed in academia and policy practice for managing oil revenues. Please describe the core logic of each rule and representative countries (if any).
3.  **Revenue Management Tools**: Provide a detailed introduction to two key revenue management tools: (1) Natural Resource Funds (NRFs), please explain their main functions, and list and explain their three main types; (2) Public Investment Management Systems, please explain why they are important for these countries, and what stages an effective system should include.
4.  **Benchmark Case Study**: Using Norway as an example, analyze its key policies and institutional arrangements for successful oil wealth management, particularly how its fiscal rules and sovereign wealth fund operate.
Please ensure your answer is well-structured, and each section is detailed and accurate.

**important**The following is a rule of highest priority that you must not violate. Please put this rule in your task plan and keep it in your memory: **During the research process, you are not allowed to view the following article and urls: {'title': 'The Policy Framework of Natural Resource Management in Oil-Dependence Countries', 'authors': ['Basem Ertimi', 'Tamat Sarmidi', 'Norlin Khalid', 'Mohd Helmi Ali'], 'urls': ['https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7099/9/1/25', 'https://www.researchgate.net/publication/347057845_The_Policy_Framework_of_Natural_Resource_Management_in_Oil-Dependence_Countries', 'https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349562167_The_Policy_Framework_of_Natural_Resource_Management_in_Oil-Dependence_Countries', 'https://ideas.repec.org/a/gam/jecomi/v9y2021i1p25-d504509.html', 'https://www.econstor.eu/handle/10419/257183', 'https://scispace.com/papers/the-policy-framework-of-natural-resource-management-in-oil-20jx4xk9e5', 'https://ouci.dntb.gov.ua/en/works/loow31El/']}. Even if you accidentally read it, please ignore the content of the article and do not quote it.**

pointwise.title: Resource curse and oil dependence
pointwise.question: Does the report define the resource curse and explain concrete economic vulnerabilities of oil dependence?

anchors.1: No meaningful definition or oil-country challenges.
anchors.2: Names the curse but treats resource abundance itself as an inevitable cause of poverty.
anchors.3: Defines adverse development outcomes and explains a relevant vulnerability, but the account is narrow.
anchors.4: Explains oil-price boom-bust exposure and revenue dependence, with a limited account of governance risks.
anchors.5: Defines the conditional development problem and connects oil-price volatility, fiscal dependence and rent-seeking or accountability risks to economic consequences.

pointwise.boundary: Dutch-disease transmission has a separate item. Do not require every historical theory or imply that all oil exporters grow poorly.

provenance.change_note: Retain distinct economic vulnerabilities without a deterministic curse.

pointwise.title: Dutch-disease transmission
pointwise.question: Does the report explain Dutch disease as a resource-boom transmission mechanism affecting other tradable sectors?

anchors.1: Absent or reverses the central mechanism.
anchors.2: Gives only the label or a generic claim that oil hurts manufacturing.
anchors.3: Resource inflows and appreciation are linked, but the consequences for non-oil export competitiveness or import demand are absent or materially unclear.
anchors.4: Explains inflows, real appreciation, non-resource competitiveness and conditional import-demand effects, with only a minor missing qualification.
anchors.5: The account explains real appreciation and/or resource-cost movement, its pressure on non-resource exports and diversification, and how higher purchasing power or relative prices can increase imports under stated conditions.

pointwise.boundary: Do not require every country's imports to rise or nominal appreciation; a qualified spending/resource-movement explanation is eligible, but conditional trade effects must actually be discussed.

provenance.change_note: Keep the causal relationship intact rather than split definition from its consequence.

pointwise.title: Permanent-income rule
pointwise.question: Does the report explain the spending basis of the permanent-income approach?

anchors.1: No substantive account of permanent-income rule.
anchors.2: Only labels or an unsupported general assertion, without an identifiable account.
anchors.3: Wealth or permanent income is named but its relation to sustainable spending is unclear.
anchors.4: The required account is concrete and its main components are present, with only minor scope or detail gaps.
anchors.5: Explains how expected long-run resource wealth informs a spending flow, with country attribution scoped if used.

pointwise.boundary: No fixed equation, estimate or compulsory country; rule risks remain PT.D1.04.

drb2_95.title: 液压成形材料与缺陷
drb2_95.full_query:
我正在调研液压成形（hydroforming）技术，希望你能帮我整理一份关于该技术在材料选择和常见制造缺陷方面的资料。请你作为一名行业分析师，完成以下两个任务：

1.  **常用材料分析**：详细梳理在液压成形工艺中几种代表性的金属材料。具体来说，请覆盖以下四种：高强度钢（HSS）、高强度铝合金、镁合金和钛合金。对于每一种材料，都请从“材料特性”、“成形挑战”和“主要应用”这三个方面进行介绍，并给出具体的应用实例（例如用在汽车的哪个部件上）。

2.  **常见缺陷、成因及对策**：总结液压成形过程中最常见的五种制造缺陷：表面缺陷（Surface defects）、回弹（Springback）、起皱（Wrinkling）、变薄（Thinning）和撕裂（Tearing）。对于每一种缺陷，请清晰地列出其“主要成因”和“建议的解决方法”。

请将你的回答分为以上两个部分，并为每个部分设置清晰的标题。内容需要准确、具体，避免模糊不清的表述。

**important**The following is a rule of highest priority that you must not violate. Please put this rule in your task plan and keep it in your memory: **During the research process, you are not allowed to view the following article and urls: {'title': 'A review of emerging hydroforming technologies: design considerations, parametric studies, and recent innovations', 'authors': ['Satish Chinchanikar', 'Harsh Mulik', 'Param Varude', 'Sameer Atole', 'Neha Mundada'], 'urls': ['https://jeas.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s44147-024-00546-z', 'https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385401108_A_review_of_emerging_hydroforming_technologies_design_considerations_parametric_studies_and_recent_innovations', 'https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024JEAS...71..205C/abstract']}. Even if you accidentally read it, please ignore the content of the article and do not quote it.**

drb2_97.title: 沉浸式梵高展
drb2_97.full_query:
你好，我最近总是看到那种沉浸式梵高艺术展的广告，感觉铺天盖地的。我有点好奇，想让你帮我做一个全面的调研，但请只关注2022年及以前的情况。我希望你帮我搞清楚几个问题：

1. 当时市面上有哪些主要的梵高沉浸式展览？请列出这些展览的具体名称及其背后的主要运营公司。
2. 这些展览里面到底是什么样的？是看真画吗？还是用投影和其他技术？它们的内容、形式和体验流程大致是怎样的？请详细描述一下，可以举一些具体的例子。
3. 这些展览的商业模式是怎样的？比如，做一个这样的展览大概要花多少钱？普通人去看一次票价是多少？它们赚钱吗，有没有具体的收入数据可以参考？
4. 社会上对这些展览的评价怎么样？我希望你从不同角度来总结，比如专业的艺术评论家是怎么看的，商业财经媒体是怎么分析的，以及普通观众和地方新闻是怎么报道的。

请你把调研结果整理成四部分，分别使用“一、主要竞争展览及其主办方”、“二、展览内容与体验”、“三、商业模式与成本收益”、“四、各方评价”作为标题。谢谢！

Please put this rule in your task plan and keep it in your memory: **During the research process, you are not allowed to view the following article and urls: {'title': 'The Influencers: Van Gogh Immersive Experiences and the Attention-Experience Economy', 'authors': ['Kate Mondloch'], 'urls': ['https://www.mdpi.com/2076-0752/11/5/90', 'https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363712184_The_Influencers_Van_Gogh_Immersive_Experiences_and_the_Attention-Experience_Economy', 'https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/2412794ee1f3960f50cdd717199b0e8524a90f13', 'https://scispace.com/papers/the-influencers-van-gogh-immersive-experiences-and-the-12hjy9kh']}. rr_683a58c9a7e7fe4e76958488.title: 记忆痕迹与预测编码模型
rr_683a58c9a7e7fe4e76958488.full_query: Propose a biologically plausible model that integrates the neuroscience concepts of engrams and predictive coding into one network capable of performing classification tasks.

pointwise.title: Engram representation
pointwise.question: Does the model specify a persistent memory trace and how reactivating it retrieves relevant stored information?

anchors.1: No memory trace is specified.
anchors.2: Engram is only a label for an arbitrary activation or class output.
anchors.3: A trace is described but what persists or how it is reactivated is materially unclear.
anchors.4: Persistent storage and reactivation of a specific memory are clear, and the trace's functional contribution is explained, with a minor gap in the causal account.
anchors.5: The model specifies what neuronal/assembly or synaptic state stores a specific memory, what persists, and how reactivation retrieves it; it explains the trace's functional contribution through an expected selective effect of perturbing it or an equivalent causal account, and distinguishes it from a transient prediction error.

pointwise.boundary: Evaluate an operational memory representation, not a mandatory sparse-assembly density, memory-system theory or one-assembly-per-class design. Persistent storage and retrieval alone, without explaining the trace's functional contribution to a specific memory, remain at 3 rather than 4/5. A predicted selective effect on that memory's retrieval, or an equivalent causal account, is sufficient; no executed perturbation experiment is required. Distributed or redundant traces are eligible: disrupting one cell need not abolish recall, and the explanation may concern a graded contribution or an appropriately scoped ensemble perturbation.

provenance.change_note: Adapt flat:3 to persistent encoding, reactivation and a trace's functional contribution to a specific memory. High anchors require a predicted selective perturbation effect or an equivalent causal explanation, not an executed experiment, fixed sparsity or nonredundant one-cell necessity. The five anchors and boundary are locally designed. For flat:9 (raw weight -3), retain the distinction between memory traces and transient errors without requiring error-controlled engram formation.

pointwise.title: Predictive-coding computation
pointwise.question: Does the model specify predictions, the mismatches they are compared with, and how those errors update its inferred state?

anchors.1: No predictive-coding computation is specified.
anchors.2: Predictive coding is named without a prediction–mismatch operation.
anchors.3: Predictions or errors are concrete, but their comparison or effect on inferred state is missing.
anchors.4: Prediction, mismatch and state-update roles are clear, with a minor signal detail missing.
anchors.5: Specifies the generative/hierarchical levels, downward predictions and upward/local mismatches, their repeated message-passing effect on inferred states, and the distinction from any global label or reward signal used.

pointwise.boundary: Equations, pseudocode or precise prose may specify the computation. Dedicated error neurons, layers or dendritic implementations are alternatives, not a checklist. Predictive coding is not satisfied by merely renaming a classifier's global loss. Levels may be populations or representational stages rather than anatomical layers; a generic one-step reconstruction loss alone does not specify iterative predictive inference.

provenance.change_note: Adapt the official material to the specific object 'Predictive-coding computation': Does the model specify predictions, the mismatches they are compared with, and how those errors update its inferred state? Locally design the five anchors and boundaries. Concrete changes: Retain predictions, mismatch and error-driven inference, allowing different biological implementations. Explicitly distinguish local mismatch from any task/reward signal actually used. Retain the actual prediction/error computation rather than a specific dedicated-neuron implementation. Retain inference/state computation without equation-only format. v3.3 makes directional and iterative inference content explicit.

pointwise.title: One integrated network
pointwise.question: Does the proposal specify how the engram and predictive-coding processes interact within the same classification network?

anchors.1: Only one concept is implemented, or the two are unrelated systems.
anchors.2: Both concepts are named but no functional connection is specified.
anchors.3: Both processes have roles, but memory-to-prediction information, mismatch-driven correction, or routing/timing in the same network is unclear.
anchors.4: The principal interaction and component roles are explicit, with one minor handoff gap.
anchors.5: Shows how reactivated or completed memory shapes predictions, and how mismatch-driven inference or learning corrects the active prediction/memory use; routing or phase conditions keep the signals interpretable in one network.

pointwise.boundary: Functional integration does not require a single cell type, shared synapses or direct error-gating of engram formation. Modular subsystems in one connected network are eligible. Merely presenting two independent classifiers is not integration. Error modulation can act on retrieval/inferred state rather than the trace-forming synapse, but a disconnected memory lookup attached after classification is not functional integration.

provenance.change_note: Adapt the official material to the specific object 'One integrated network': Does the proposal specify how the engram and predictive-coding processes interact within the same classification network? Locally design the five anchors and boundaries. Concrete changes: Retain the functional single-network coupling, not same-synapse error gating or neuromodulatory phase routing. Raw weight is -3. Preserve the concern about conflating traces with errors or failing to integrate, but do not mandate error-controlled engram formation. Map connections to integration, update specification to learning, and class interface to classification; do not copy the entire architecture checklist into each child. v3.3 restores memory-conditioned predictions, correction and routing without requiring shared-synapse error gating.

pointwise.title: Class output procedure
pointwise.question: Does the model specify how a new input produces a class decision?

anchors.1: No class decision procedure.
anchors.2: It states that the model classifies but gives no readout.
anchors.3: A readout is identified but the path from inferred/retrieved state to a label is unclear, or test-time supervision is not distinguished.
anchors.4: Input-to-class decision is explicit, with a minor readout or stopping detail missing.
anchors.5: The proposal specifies input encoding, the usable inference/retrieval state and how a class decision is read from it; training labels are not implicitly required for an unseen input's answer.

pointwise.boundary: No fixed decoder, confidence metric, dataset or accuracy target is mandatory. This is a proposal, not a demand for an executed benchmark. Class readout detail is distinct from the memory–prediction interface.

provenance.change_note: Adapt the official material to the specific object 'Class output procedure': Does the model specify how a new input produces a class decision? Locally design the five anchors and boundaries. Concrete changes: Retain an explicit class decision path, not a prescribed decoder. Map connections to integration, update specification to learning, and class interface to classification; do not copy the entire architecture checklist into each child.

pointwise.title: Memory formation and learning updates
pointwise.question: Does the model specify how experience forms/updates memory and the learned quantities needed for predictive classification?

anchors.1: No formation or learning process is described.
anchors.2: Only a named learning rule is given.
anchors.3: Updates are partly specified, but trace allocation/diversity, maintenance of persistent memory, or a necessary predictive-learning signal/phase is missing.
anchors.4: Required formation and updates are specified, with only a minor signal/phase gap.
anchors.5: Specifies update targets, driving signals and learning versus inference phases; explains how traces are initially or online allocated, how distinct memories avoid collapse onto the same state, and how required persistent traces survive subsequent updates.

pointwise.boundary: Learning equations and precise procedural descriptions are equally eligible. Engrams need not all be fixed at initialization; Hebbian, three-factor or other justified rules are not universally required. Specify a necessary update rather than invoke its name. pointwise.title: Local biological computation and signal access

anchors.3: Some computations are mapped, but a central update requires an unexplained nonlocal signal, timing or learning-phase access.
anchors.4: Essential signals, access and timing are explained, with a minor implementation qualification missing.
anchors.5: Maps comparison and plasticity operations to neural/synaptic processes, specifies which signals are locally available and when, and gives a credible account of any broadcast/modulatory signal or phase separation actually required.

pointwise.boundary: No universal ban or endorsement of backpropagation. A required global quantity needs a concrete biological access account, not merely an acknowledged idealization. Wiring and activity regulation are checked separately; no fixed neuromodulator or gating architecture is imposed.

anchors.5: Main content contributes to the proposed classifier, its biological interpretation or a necessary limitation/test; unfamiliar concepts have an explained role.

pointwise.title: Circuit wiring constraints

anchors.1: No circuit structure is specified.
anchors.2: Only brain-region or neuron names are provided.
anchors.3: Population roles or pathways are described, but an essential connection or a wiring assumption required by the proposed computation is unexplained.
anchors.4: Essential population roles, pathways and relevant wiring assumptions are clear, with a minor implementation gap.
anchors.5: Specifies how the chosen populations and connections carry the required signals, and explains the biological implementation or bounded approximation of the wiring assumptions on which this model depends.

pointwise.boundary: Do not require every model to enumerate connection density, weight symmetry, long-range projections or a particular circuit architecture. pointwise.title: Computational evaluation specification

pointwise.boundary: A proposed experiment or concrete worked test is sufficient; completed results are not required. Train/test partitioning, ablations, uncertainty statistics and biological experiments are not universal checklist requirements. If a proposed claim relies on generalization, component attribution or a particular comparison, the supporting test must explain the corresponding conditions; a worked example alone does not establish generalization. Optional biological testing is compared in PW.D4.biotest, not required as a separate pointwise deliverable.

rr_6847465956a0f6376a605363.title: Turo and Getaround: performance, valuation and employment
rr_6847465956a0f6376a605363.full_query: Write a brief research report comparing the performance of the car rental companies Turo and Getaround, detailing all major economic events for each company from 2020 to 2025 and how it affected the company's valuation. If the company falls in valuation, be sure to explain how it happened and its effects on employee numbers. Write the report for an audience not familiar with US economics and venture capital.

pointwise.title: Turo's economic event history
pointwise.question: Does the report cover Turo's major economic developments across 2020–2025 with dates and business consequences?

anchors.1: No usable Turo history is provided.
anchors.2: Only isolated headlines appear, without a meaningful period-wide account.
anchors.3: Several events are described, but a major phase or economically consequential development is omitted or undated.
anchors.4: The main developments and consequences are clear, with only a minor timing or event-context gap.
anchors.5: The period's consequential developments are dated and explained, including material changes in financing/listing plans and operating performance; coverage is not merely a count of headlines.

pointwise.boundary: Use the IPO effort and withdrawal, expansion/profitability developments and 2025 restructuring as supplied coverage leads, not independently verified facts. The report must address materially relevant developments through its stated 2025 endpoint. Do not demand every official example, including incidents with no established economic effect.

query_quotes: all major economic events for each company from 2020 to 2025
provenance.change_note: Adapt event coverage into a period-wide account; remove the two-event quota and mandatory examples. Anchors are locally designed.

pointwise.title: Getaround's economic event history
pointwise.question: Does the report cover Getaround's major economic developments across 2020–2025 with dates and business consequences?

anchors.1: No usable Getaround history is provided.
anchors.2: Only a failure label or isolated event is mentioned.
anchors.3: There is an event history, but a major financing, listing or operating phase is absent or lacks its consequence.
anchors.4: Main phases and consequences are clear, with a minor timing or transition gap.
anchors.5: The account covers consequential financing, public-listing and operating changes over the period, including material retrenchment, with clear dates and business consequences, distinguishing supported explanations from uncertain attribution.

pointwise.boundary: Pandemic disruption, funding, SPAC listing, subsequent financial stress and US operating exit are supplied coverage leads; clarify scope and supporting evidence rather than treating this list as verified. Listing valuation is separately assessed; no two-event quota. The reverse-merger funding or unit-economics expectations and later US exit are not a compulsory explanatory chain. An evidence-supported account of the major events and their consequences can satisfy this item without that narrative; missing major events or consequences still affects the score. PW.D3.01 compares the reasoning of the explanations actually offered, rather than rewarding a prescribed story.

query_quotes: all major economic events for each company from 2020 to 2025
provenance.change_note: Review 31: remove the mandatory reverse-merger-expectations-to-US-exit narrative from levels 3 and 5, retaining period-wide major-event coverage, dates, consequences and attribution limits. Align with the existing PW.D3.01 boundary.

pointwise.title: Turo valuation evidence and gaps

anchors.1: No valuation information or explicit evidence gap is given.
anchors.2: A dollar figure is supplied without date, basis or explanation of what it measures.
anchors.3: There are dated figures or gaps, but a major private-round, secondary estimate or hoped-for IPO distinction is unclear. An absent opening valuation basis or unsupported claim that no event valuation is available is an important gap.
anchors.4: Main valuation figures and evidence gaps have clear dates and bases, with only a minor qualification missing.
anchors.5: Material event-linked valuations or well-supported disclosure gaps are stated, separating completed financing valuations, secondary estimates and listing expectations; no continuous private-company market price is invented. Establish the opening valuation context and distinguish an actual measured change from undisclosed values or expectations.

pointwise.boundary: Do not require the supplied $1.24B, $1.7B or $2.2B figures. A financing amount is not a company valuation; abandoned IPO plans do not alone establish a measured fall. A supported gap can fully answer an unavailable valuation.

query_quotes: how it affected the company's valuation
provenance.change_note: Retain limited private valuation visibility and basis distinctions; remove fixed figures and unverified round dates. Anchors are local. v3.3 requires opening context, not the unverified exact unicorn date.

rr_6847465956a0f6376a605371.title: Three relocation cities for a remote engineer
rr_6847465956a0f6376a605371.full_query:
i'm a remote software engineer in SF. its getting too expensive. i make $120k. i want to relocate somewhere else in the US. i need you to do the research for me and give me a ranked list of your top 3 cities.

here are my non-negotaibles:
- the cost of living HAS to be at least 30% lower than sf. especially rent and healthcare
- since i'm remote, I need high speed and reliable internet connection
- i really don't want to be stuck in a car. i need a walkable neighborhood (like a walk score over 60?) and easy access to green spaces or nature for hiking
- I also need a major airport within about 90 minutes

can you write up a detailed report for me? i need them ranked with good justifications. please also include the trade-offs like what's the weather really like, what are the state tax implications (huge for me coming from CA), diversity, amenities, that kind of stuff

it's important this is backed by real data, not just vibes. like use actual cost of living indexes, real estate data, internet speed rankings, ect

pointwise.title: Three ranked US destinations
pointwise.question: Does the report give an identifiable top three US cities with reasons for their order?

anchors.1: No usable US relocation shortlist.
anchors.2: Only one city, or an unranked collection with no usable recommendation.
anchors.3: Only two US cities are substantively ranked, or three are ranked or discussed but an important ranking reason or a concrete user-relevant downside for any city is missing.
anchors.4: Three US cities are ranked with clear reasons and concrete user-relevant trade-offs for each, with only minor explanation gaps.
anchors.5: Three US cities are explicitly ranked by suitability, with grounded reasons and concrete user-relevant trade-offs for each that explain the recommendation rather than claiming universal superiority.

pointwise.boundary: Any cities may qualify; no geographic-spread requirement and no preference for Austin, Raleigh or Salt Lake City. If fewer than three can be substantiated, an honest shortfall remains incomplete coverage, not a reason to invent a third. Reason persuasiveness is PW.D4.01.

query_quotes: a ranked list of your top 3 cities
provenance.change_note: Merge ranking, reasons and negative missing-city check; preserve US scope but drop example cities and regional diversity.

pointwise.title: Thirty-percent total-cost constraint

anchors.2: Only labels or an unsupported general assertion, without an identifiable account.
anchors.3: A city lacks a comparable total-cost result or the reduction threshold is not established.
anchors.4: The required account is concrete and its main components are present, with only minor scope or detail gaps.
anchors.5: Uses an explicit SF baseline and comparable city totals or indexes to establish at least 30% reduction for every recommendation; dates and scope are clear.

pointwise.boundary: Below-threshold or merely conditional options cannot earn 4/5. A city-by-city diagnostic record is required; rent alone does not establish total reduction.

provenance.change_note: Main-agent v3.5: split this object from PT.D1.02; sibling content cannot compensate. Source links indicate adaptation, not literal preservation.

anchors.4: The required account is concrete and its main components are present, with only minor scope or detail gaps.
anchors.5: Provides interpretable rent amounts with comparable housing basis, period and geographic scope for SF and all three destinations.

pointwise.boundary: Actual data accuracy is D2; healthcare remains PT.D1.03. Record each city separately in the rationale, without inventing fixed recommended cities.

rr_6847465956a0f6376a6053a0.title: 分布式音频与聊天
rr_6847465956a0f6376a6053a0.full_query: Write a technical proposal for a distributed audio streaming system. The system should include an audio streaming platform and a live chat feature. This application should be built for both browser and mobile settings. Include detailed technologies and justify why they are used. Assume the audience is a team of experienced software developers at a medium sized software company.

pointwise.title: Proposal objective and assumptions
pointwise.question: Does the proposal state its audio-and-chat product objective and the workload, performance, operating and team assumptions needed to interpret its design?

anchors.1: Neither an identifiable audio-and-chat objective nor usable design assumptions is stated.
anchors.2: Only a generic objective is given, or assumptions are listed without identifying the product they describe.
anchors.3: The product is identifiable, but an important workload, performance, operating or team assumption needed to interpret its choices is missing or too vague.
anchors.4: The objective and the assumptions needed by the design are clear, with only a minor interpretive gap.
anchors.5: The objective and necessary workload, performance, operating and team assumptions are explicit. Performance expectations are concrete enough to assess the chosen design, and team capabilities or availability relied on by the proposal are stated.

pointwise.boundary: Judge the context needed to interpret this proposal, not the ambition of its targets. Concrete expectations may be numeric or a testable behavior; no prescribed latency, uptime, team size or staffing model is required. Goals and the conditions that give them meaning remain one item. Feasibility, cost and implementation priorities are assessed separately. A missing assumption matters only when a material choice depends on it.

provenance.change_note: 从指定三题小修baseline保留问题与锚点；来源精确恢复自official_checks逐项表，非将官方整组复制到所有子项。

pointwise.title: Audio delivery path
pointwise.question: Does the proposal specify how audio reaches a playing client, including the transport and media-handling choices at the relevant handoffs?

anchors.1: No audio delivery path is specified.
anchors.2: Audio tools are named, but the proposal does not show how they move playable audio to a client.
anchors.3: Part of the path is described, but a major origin-to-player handoff or its transport/media-handling choice is unspecified.
anchors.4: The main path, component roles and transport/media-handling choices are explicit, with only a minor handoff detail missing.
anchors.5: The chosen origin, processing if used, delivery and playback form an explicit path. The proposal identifies how audio is represented or encoded and transported, and where serving, relaying or caching is handled as relevant to that path.

pointwise.boundary: Check whether the audio path and its selected technologies are described, not whether they are better than another design. No particular live/VOD model, codec, protocol, media server, cache or CDN is required. Managed handling can satisfy the item when the proposal explains what is delegated and how the client receives compatible audio. Do not require a catalogue of alternatives; reasons for choices remain PT.D1.06.

pointwise.question: Does the proposal describe concrete audio-related and chat service interactions using its chosen API or messaging style?

pointwise.question: Does the proposal specify protections for the access boundaries, sensitive data and abuse risks created by its chosen audio-and-chat design?

anchors.2: Security tools or slogans are listed without identifying what they protect.

rr_6847465956a0f6376a605427.title: Washington, DC Independence Day 2025 itinerary
rr_6847465956a0f6376a605427.full_query: I want to create a plan for July 4, 2025, i.e., Independence Day in Washington DC. I would like an itinerary of all the things to do and all the activities that are planned for Independence Day. Create a plan for the whole day and also extend it to the weekend, if required. Provide some reviews or explain why one should visit the place or engage in the activity. Add any additional information that is required.

pointwise.title: Correct holiday and destination
pointwise.question: Does the itinerary consistently plan for Independence Day in Washington, DC on July 4, 2025?

anchors.1: The main plan is for another date or destination.
anchors.2: Several central activities belong to another year or a different trip, changing the requested plan.
anchors.3: The main destination/date is correct but a material activity has an unclear or mismatched year or location.
anchors.4: The itinerary is aligned with DC and July 4, 2025, with only a minor date/location ambiguity.
anchors.5: The main day is explicitly July 4, 2025 in DC; nearby extensions are clearly identified and other-year information is not presented as the 2025 schedule.

pointwise.boundary: Judge material recommendations, not incidental mentions of another city. Nearby Maryland/Virginia options are not automatically out of scope. A past recurring event is not proof it ran in 2025.

provenance.change_note: Adapts negative-weight geography/year checks into correct-scope anchors; rejects penalties for merely mentioning a city.

pointwise.title: Whole-day itinerary
pointwise.question: Does the report provide a sequenced morning-to-evening itinerary with usable activity time blocks and a post-event departure window?

anchors.1: No usable itinerary.
anchors.2: Only a short list or a small part of the day is planned.
anchors.3: A broad day is sketched but a major period, main activity duration or evening departure window is missing.
anchors.4: The morning-to-evening sequence and main activity windows are clear, with a minor scheduling detail missing.
anchors.5: A coherent full-day schedule gives interpretable starts and ends or durations for main activities, includes practical pacing, and continues through the evening event and departure rather than ending at its start.

pointwise.boundary: No mandatory 9 AM/10 PM bounds, four-stop minimum or named restaurant list. Transit estimates are PT.D1.05; internal feasibility is PW.D3.01. Lunch/dinner choices are now PT.D1.11; do not double-penalize their absence here. Exact 9 AM/10 PM bounds remain nonmandatory, but an evening plan ending at fireworks start is incomplete.

provenance.change_note: Retains full-day scheduling and practical pacing, relaxes imposed clock bounds and restaurants. v3.3 separates meals and clarifies evening completion.

pointwise.title: Holiday activities and event status
pointwise.question: Does the report identify a useful range of planned Independence Day activities and distinguish the chosen itinerary from alternatives?

anchors.1: No Independence Day activities.
anchors.2: Only generic sightseeing or an unspecified holiday celebration.
anchors.3: Some holiday events are concrete, but a major civic/parade, concert/live celebration or evening fireworks part of the program is omitted without an evidenced reason, or 2025 status/timing is materially unclear.
anchors.4: The main civic, live-celebration and fireworks program is covered with usable locations/status, with a minor timing or access uncertainty.
anchors.5: Provides an overview of the main civic/parade or historical commemoration, concert/live celebration and evening fireworks opportunities, with 2025 status, locations and scheduled time information; selected stops and incompatible alternatives are separated.

pointwise.boundary: Do not require attendance at all listed events or one named parade/concert. A category unavailable in 2025 may be explained with evidence, not silently removed. Fireworks timing must use applicable 2025 information, not an unverified fixed 9 PM. A scoped route cannot redefine the broader holiday program as just its chosen stops.

query_quotes: all the activities that are planned for Independence Day
provenance.change_note: Adapts recurring-event coverage into a scoped 2025 program and usable selection; avoids impossible exhaustive attendance. v3.3 restores program-category breadth and actual fireworks start information without fixed event names or clock values.

anchors.2: Only generic praise such as amazing or must-see.
anchors.3: Some stops have useful reasons, but major recommendations are unexplained or reviews are unattributed.
anchors.4: Most main recommendations have concrete appeal or attributed review context, with a minor gap.
anchors.5: The main recommendations have specific historical, experiential or other relevant reasons, or identifiable review perspectives, allowing the visitor to understand their appeal.

pointwise.boundary: Reasons are an alternative to reviews; no compulsory rating site, promotional claim or personal experience. A review is not required for every minor transfer.

query_quotes: Provide some reviews or explain why
provenance.change_note: Retains reasons/reviews as alternatives; no fixed example or sentence count.

anchors.5: Main stop-to-stop movements identify a usable travel mode and approximate travel/buffer allowance; long-distance extensions and the evening exit are accounted for.

pointwise.boundary: No exact fare, transit line or travel app is mandatory. Estimates need conditions, not false precision. Feasibility of the entire timetable is compared separately.

pointwise.title: Why prioritize LiDAR
pointwise.question: Does the report state a concrete system-design rationale for prioritizing LiDAR?

anchors.1: No rationale or a fundamentally false choice claim.
anchors.2: Only calls LiDAR accurate or safe.
anchors.3: Names a useful capability but does not connect it to the system's perception need.
anchors.4: Connects a concrete capability to the system need, with a minor scope ambiguity.
anchors.5: Clearly connects LiDAR capability to a stated perception/design need and explains why that benefit matters for this priority.

pointwise.boundary: Coverage of hardware variants, pipeline, compute, latency, energy, cost and mitigation is checked in05–14, not repeated here. This item asks why the stated capability motivates the choice, not how many constraints were listed.

provenance.change_note: v3.3 targeted revision: Remove integration-cost and limitation completeness from old high anchors; these are now direct independent content objects.

anchors.3: Names a benefit but does not connect it to the system's perception or deployment need.
anchors.4: Connects a concrete camera/learning benefit to the system need, with a minor scope ambiguity.
anchors.5: Clearly explains why the visual information or learned-perception capability motivates the chosen priority for a stated system need.

pointwise.boundary: The detailed inference pipeline is05 and deployment economics11; do not penalize their omissions here again. Camera depth need not be purely learned; no fixed brand.

anchors.3: Does not explicitly make the false claim, but the architecture relationship remains ambiguous.
anchors.4: Clearly recognizes LiDAR systems can use cameras and learning, with only minor ambiguous shorthand.
anchors.5: Clearly distinguishes sensor choice from perception software and explains that LiDAR-equipped systems can also use cameras and neural networks; the comparison concerns priorities or sensor suites rather than incompatible categories.

pointwise.boundary: Fusion-stage taxonomy is optional. Acknowledging coexistence does not require advocating sensor fusion.
